Explanation: The selectable unit is a bookable travel service such as a stay, flight, car, cruise or activity that can be distributed through Expedia Group channels or embedded partner channels.
This case models Expedia Group’s travel marketplace and B2B distribution layer, not only the Expedia.com consumer storefront.
Expedia Group has to aggregate fragmented travel supply and make it searchable, bookable and serviceable across both its own brands and outside partner channels.
Expedia earns transaction economics from merchant and agency bookings while expanding volume through direct consumer brands and B2B distribution.
The platform must keep prices, availability, payments, servicing and supplier rules consistent across many travel categories, markets and partner interfaces.
Expedia normalizes supplier inventory, exposes it to travelers and partners, and processes bookings under merchant or agency models depending on the product and contract.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Search / Book — Travelers send trip intent and booking requests into Expedia Group directly or through an Expedia-powered partner experience. | ← Provider · Inventory / Rates — Travel suppliers contribute bookable capacity, prices, schedules, policies and availability to the marketplace. | → Provider · Bookings / Pay — Expedia Group sends reservations and demand to suppliers and, under merchant flows, can collect traveler funds and later pay the supplier; agency flows can be settled differently. | → Partner · Inventory / API — Expedia Group exposes travel inventory, rates, booking functions and service capabilities to B2B distributors through Rapid, white-label and other partner products. | ← Partner · Demand / Bookings — B2B distributors bring their own customer demand and booking volume back into Expedia Group’s marketplace infrastructure.

Explanation: Expedia sets distribution, display, booking, payment, servicing and partner requirements while suppliers retain responsibility for the underlying travel service.
Demand is reached through Expedia Group consumer brands and through the customer channels of B2B partners.
Core activities include search and merchandising, booking and payment processing, customer service, fraud controls, supplier connectivity and partner enablement.
Key resources include global travel supply, traveler demand, first-party data, pricing and booking systems, service operations and distribution technology.
Travelers are people booking leisure, family or business travel either directly on an Expedia Group brand or through a partner-powered travel experience.
Travelers want to find and reserve the travel components needed for a trip without managing separate supplier systems.
Travelers gain broad inventory, comparison, bundled trip options, standardized booking flows and support across multiple travel categories.
Travel planning is naturally fragmented across airlines, hotels, cars, activities, policies and payment rules.
Travelers submit dates, destinations and preferences and create bookings either on Expedia-branded channels or through an Expedia-powered partner experience.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Search / Book — Travelers send trip intent and booking requests into Expedia Group directly or through an Expedia-powered partner experience. | ← Provider · Travel Service — The supplier delivers the actual stay, flight, car, cruise or activity to the traveler.

Explanation: Travelers narrow supply by destination, dates, party size, price, category, schedule, amenities and other trip preferences.
Travelers can enter through Expedia Group websites and apps or through a partner-owned interface powered by Expedia Group technology or supply.
Travelers compare options, book, pay where applicable, manage changes and ultimately consume the travel service supplied by the provider.
Travelers contribute trip intent, dates, preferences, attention, identity and payment capability.
Providers are hotels and vacation-rental operators, airlines, car-rental firms, cruise operators, activity businesses and other companies that deliver the underlying travel service.
Suppliers want to turn perishable rooms, seats, cars and activity capacity into paid bookings while managing rates and availability.
Expedia Group can expose supplier inventory across its consumer brands and a much wider B2B distribution network.
Suppliers give up margin or commission and must manage channel economics, availability, cancellations, content accuracy and distribution rules.
Suppliers provide rates, availability and bookable inventory; Expedia earns margin or commission depending on the merchant or agency model and contract.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Inventory / Rates — Travel suppliers contribute bookable capacity, prices, schedules, policies and availability to the marketplace. | ← Owner · Bookings / Pay — Expedia Group sends reservations and demand to suppliers and, under merchant flows, can collect traveler funds and later pay the supplier; agency flows can be settled differently. | → Consumer · Travel Service — The supplier delivers the actual stay, flight, car, cruise or activity to the traveler.

Explanation: Suppliers must meet commercial, technical, content, legal and service requirements for the relevant travel category.
Suppliers connect through Expedia Group partner tools, connectivity providers and APIs appropriate to their product category.
Suppliers maintain inventory and pricing, accept reservations and deliver the hotel stay, flight, car, cruise or activity.
Providers contribute the actual travel capacity, rates, schedules, content, policies and service operations.
Partners are airlines, banks, travel agencies, online retailers, corporate travel platforms and other businesses that distribute Expedia Group travel supply to their own customers.
These businesses want to add a travel-shopping and booking capability without building a global supply network and servicing stack from scratch.
Travel can create an additional revenue stream, deepen loyalty and make an existing customer relationship more useful.
Partners need reliable inventory, fast integrations, booking support, payments and servicing that work inside their own customer experience.
Partners bring traveler demand and booking requests into Expedia Group’s B2B layer and receive travel supply, rates and reservation capabilities in return.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Inventory / API — Expedia Group exposes travel inventory, rates, booking functions and service capabilities to B2B distributors through Rapid, white-label and other partner products. | → Owner · Demand / Bookings — B2B distributors bring their own customer demand and booking volume back into Expedia Group’s marketplace infrastructure.

Explanation: Expedia Group reviews prospective B2B partners and applies commercial, technical, brand and launch requirements to the selected solution.
Partners can use Rapid APIs, Expedia TAAP, white-label technology and co-branded solutions depending on their business model.
Partners merchandise travel to their customers, manage the front-end relationship and coordinate booking or service flows with Expedia Group.
Partners contribute established customer relationships, traffic, loyalty ecosystems, distribution channels and brand context.
